yt.title: How GPS knows where you are #Shorts
yt.description:
A 30-second look at how satellite navigation works.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.text: How GPS knows where you are
scenes.narration: How does your phone know where you are? It is really a timing problem.

scenes.text: Each satellite broadcasts the exact time its signal left.
scenes.narration: Each GPS satellite continuously broadcasts its position and the exact time the signal was sent.

scenes.text: Radio travels at the speed of light. Delay becomes distance.
scenes.narration: Radio waves travel at the speed of light, so the delay of the signal tells your phone how far away the satellite is.

scenes.label: Distance light travels in one nanosecond, in centimeters
scenes.caption: A clock error of one billionth of a second is a thirty centimeter error.
scenes.narration: In one billionth of a second, light travels about thirty centimeters. So the clocks have to be extremely precise.

scenes.text: Three distances fix a position. A fourth fixes your phone's clock.
scenes.narration: Three satellites are enough to fix a position in space. A fourth lets the receiver correct its own cheap clock.
